title: Great Britain 1822-1827, monthly: share price indices (Gayer, Rostow and Schwartz; Hayek), Bank Rate, the rate of discount on three-month prime bills, the yield on consols and wholesale prices
source: Bank of England, 'A millennium of macroeconomic data for the UK' (version 3.1): sheet 'M13. Monthly Share Price Indices in the UK 1709-2015' (Gayer, Rostow and Schwarz (1953) index, 1811-1850, 63 companies, inclusive of mines and excluding mines, June 1840 = 100, weighted by numbers of shares/paid up capital; Hayek's index of share prices, 1820-1868, unweighted, 1841 = 100), sheet 'M9. Monthly short-term interest rates, 1694-2016' (Bank Rate, end month, from sheet D1 Official rates; the rate of discount for three month prime or first class bills 1824-1939, Overend Gurney quoted in the 1857 Select Committee on Bank Acts, monthly average of weekly data) sheet 'M10. Monthly long-term interest rates, 1753-2016' (yield on 3% consols 1823-1860, Odlyzko (2014), monthly average of weekly observations) and sheet 'M6. Mthly prices and wages' (wholesale prices of domestic and imported commodities 1790-1850, Gayer et al. 1953, 1821-5 = 100)
series: year, month (1-12); shares_incl_mines, shares_excl_mines: the Gayer-Rostow-Schwartz indices (June 1840 = 100); shares_hayek: Hayek's index (1841 = 100); bank_rate: Bank Rate, per cent a year, end of month; prime_bills_rate: rate of discount on three-month prime bills, per cent a year, monthly average of weekly data (empty before 1824 and where the sheet has no value); consol_yield: yield on 3% consols, per cent a year, monthly average of weekly observations (empty before 1823); wholesale_1821_25: the Gayer-Rostow-Schwartz wholesale price index (1821-5 = 100)
license: The workbook asks users to cite the underlying sources ('When using this data, please cite this source'). The Bank of England publishes it as a research dataset; a subset is stored here for teaching, with attribution to the Bank of England and to the authors of the series.
notes: Workbook SHA-256 4c23dd392a498691eac92659aec283fb43f28118bd80511dc87fc595974195eb (the copy used for boe_millennium_gb_1790_1830). The script checks the headings of each column it reads (rows 3-7 of the sheets; for the consol yield, the description, the source 'Odlyzko (2014)' and the note 'Monthly average of weekly observations') and fails if one has moved. The sheet spells the authors 'Gayer, Rostow and Schwarz'. The index of shares inclusive of mines includes the mining companies formed in 1824-1825; the chapter compares it with the index excluding mines to show the mania in mining shares. Bank Rate was 4 per cent from 1822 (Tooke: the Bank 'reduced its rate of discount from 5 to 4 per cent' in the summer of 1822, say_facts row tk2_rate) and was raised to 5 per cent in the crisis of December 1825; the usury laws prohibited interest above 5 per cent (Cannan, bullion_facts rows cn_usury5 and cn_usury), so that the Bank could not raise its rate above 5.
citation: Gayer, A. D., W. W. Rostow and A. J. Schwartz (1953), The Growth and Fluctuation of the British Economy 1790-1850, Oxford: Clarendon Press; Report from the Select Committee on the Bank Acts (1857), evidence of Overend, Gurney and Co.; Odlyzko, A. (2014), the consol yields 1823-1860 as compiled in the workbook; data via Bank of England, A Millennium of Macroeconomic Data for the UK, v3.1 (R. Thomas and N. Dimsdale, 2017)
